newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit Lyonnais targets higher core profitability.
newsitem.headline: Credit Lyonnais targets higher core profitability.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais has set a target of higher pre-tax profitability in 1997 despite the impact of likely new interest rate cuts on its domestic French margins, chairman Jean Peyrelevade said on Friday.
"We continue to budget in 1997 for lower margins but this does not prevent us having a target of significantly increasing pre-tax profitability," he told reporters at a press gathering.

Higher volumes in 1996 were not enough to make up for lower rates, which he said had a negative impact on a deposit bank. Rate reductions were more than the bank budgeted for last year, costing a billion francs in lost potential revenue, he said.
He said net banking income had slipped again in 1996 but he hoped it would stabilise this year and start rising in 1998.
The current financial year would benefit from a reorganisation of the bank's small-business activities.
"This is a market in which we will lose a little more money in 1996. In our 1997 budget, we stop losing," he said.
He said the reduction in net banking income in France had masked the "basic work" carried out by the bank in improving its profitability through job reductions and risk management.
All it needed was for net banking income to stabilise to get a leverage effect and push the bank into profitability.
"The day net bank income stabilises in France, I can't tell you the take-off that we will get," he said.
